message.description: For people; it may change. It states what was wrong and how to fix it.

param.description: The JSON Pointer of the field at fault within the request body, if any.

anyOf.description: 400: the body is not valid JSON, or the request envelope is wrong.

400: the job input or settings do not parse or validate. The errors found, at least one,
each tied to a field; not necessarily every error.

422: the input parses, but uses a feature this service does not offer. One error per field
whose value is not available, at least one.
401: missing, unknown, expired, or revoked credential.
402: the available balance does not cover the job's hold.
403: the account is suspended.
404: no such resource for this account.
405: the path exists, but not with this method; `Allow` lists the methods it takes.

406: the response needs an encoding the request's `Accept-Encoding` does not take, such as
compression for live search.
409: the idempotency key was used for a different request.
409: the job has not ended yet; stop it first.
410: the job document was deleted at its expiry.
412: the project changed since the version in `If-Match`.
413: the request body exceeds the size limit.
422: the request exceeds a limit.
428: a project save or deletion without `If-Match`.
429: too many requests or queued jobs; `Retry-After` gives seconds.
500: server failure.
503: temporarily unavailable; `Retry-After` gives seconds.

ApiError.description: What went wrong with a request.

oneOf.description:
At least 3 points, in either winding; a last point equal to the first is allowed. The
edges must not cross each other.
An axis-aligned rectangle with positive `width` and `height`.

A contour of segments, meant for curves; `Contour::Polygon` is the compact form for
straight edges. Each segment runs from the previous segment's end, or `start`, to its own
end, and a path that does not end at `start` is closed by a straight line. It must not
cross itself; an error names the segments that cross.

charged.description: The charge, once the job ends.

held.description: The current hold, released when the job ends.

anyOf.description:
The search found no placement for the part on any empty sheet; its movable copies are
left unplaced. It means none was found, not that none exists.

A locked placement reaches outside its sheet, overlaps another locked placement, a sheet
hole, or a defect, or comes closer to them than the separations allow; it is kept as given.
`path` points to the placement in the input.

A hole of the part's geometry reaches outside its outer contour, overlaps another hole, or
splits the part into pieces; it is ignored, so the part is solid there. `hole_index`
indexes the geometry's holes.

The boundary separation lay between 0 and half the parts' separation and was raised to
half of it.

Diagnostic.description: A fallback the import took. With `OnInputError::Fail`, any of them fails the job instead.

Engine.description: The engine that ran a job.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error response.

FieldError.description: An error in one field of invalid input.

param.description: The JSON Pointer of the field at fault.

Geometry.description:
A shape that any number of parts and sheets may use. A geometry is never altered: fallbacks
apply to the part or sheet that uses it.

HoleMode.description: Whether other parts may be placed in a part's holes, locked copies included.

Input.description: The input a client submits: one complete nesting problem.

geometries.description: The shapes that parts and sheets refer to, nonempty.

parts.description: What is to be produced, nonempty.

Job.description:
The job resource: the light view of a job for polling and lists, without its input and outcome,
which the full `JobDocument` holds.

diagnostics.description: The fallbacks the import took; absent in lists.

document_expires_at.description: When the job document is deleted, 30 days after the job ends; `None` until then.

settings.description: Including the values the service chose, such as the seed.

JobDocument.description:
The self-contained record of a job, from input to outcome. It holds the job's own data only:
credits, timestamps, and the job's ID belong to the API's job resource.

outcome.description: Present only for a completed job.

run.description: Present once the job has started.

param.description: The JSON Pointer of the field at fault, if any, within the request body.

anyOf.description:
The worker's import refused the input: with `OnInputError::Fail`, a fallback would have
been needed. The errors found, at least one, each tied to a field.
The search ended before it found any feasible solution.
The time limit ran out during import, before any search.
The worker stopped responding.
The job could not be run, such as one not started within 24 hours.

JobError.description: Why a job failed, in the shape of an API error.

JobList.description: One page of a list, ordered by the listed timestamp, ties broken by ID.

next_cursor.description: The cursor for the next page; `None` on the last page.

JobSettings.description:
The settings a job is submitted with. The service fills in the rest, as recorded in the job's
`Settings`.

auto_termination.description: End the search early once it stops improving; `false` when absent.

seed.description: From 0 to 2⁵³ − 1; chosen by the service when absent.

time_limit_seconds.description:
The maximum solver time, from 1 up to the account's
`max_time_limit_seconds`. It sets the job's credit
hold.

JobStatus.description:
A job's status, the filter of `GET /v1/jobs`. Statuses are closed: a new one needs a new API
version.

Layout.description:
The placements on one opened sheet. Sheets of one entry repeat its `sheet_id`; their order
tells them apart. A layout that completes a locked layout starts with its placements,
unchanged and in their input order.

consumed_area.description:
The sheet's material in use: the area of its outline left of `cut_x`, minus the area its
holes cover, with defects counted as consumed.

cut_x.description:
Where the last opened sheet is cut, as an x coordinate in the sheet's own coordinates: the
parts lie left of it, the boundary separation included. `None` for the sheets before the
last, which are used in full.

placed_area.description: The material area of the placed parts, locked ones included.

Limit.description: A limit that a request exceeded.

LimitName.description: The name of a limit; those in `Limits` carry its field's name.

max_part_copies.description: The most part copies in one job input.

max_project_bytes.description: The total size of the account's project documents.

max_queued_jobs.description: The most queued jobs; beyond them, submission is rate limited.

max_running_jobs.description: The most jobs running at once; further jobs wait as queued.

LockedLayout.description:
Given placements on one sheet, which the solver completes.

- Each locked layout takes the next unused sheet of its entry, in input order; an entry with
  fewer sheets than locked layouts is invalid.
- Each placement uses up one copy of its part; a part with fewer copies than locked
  placements is invalid.
- A sheet holding a locked layout, and every sheet before it, is opened.
- Placements stand as given, also when they conflict, see
  `Diagnostic::LockedPlacementConflict`. They
  are not checked against the part's permitted orientations.

boundary.description:
Between a part and the edge of its material, a sheet hole, or a defect. A value between 0
and half of `parts` is raised to half of `parts`, with
`Diagnostic::BoundarySeparationRaised`.

parts.description: Between any two parts, also between a part and the edge of another part's hole it lies in.

OnInputError.description: What happens to input that cannot be used as given.

oneOf.description: Used with a fallback and reported as a `Diagnostic`.
The job fails instead, with `invalid_job_input` and the errors listed.

Orientation.description:
The permitted orientations of a part's copies: every combination of a permitted reflection
and a permitted rotation.

reflection.description:
Nonempty and without repeats. A mirror across another axis is the x-axis mirror plus a
rotation.

Outcome.description: The result of a completed job.

unplaced.description:
Per part with copies not placed. For every part, its quantity equals its placed copies,
locked ones included, plus its unplaced copies.

Part.description: Something to produce, in copies that cannot be told apart.

quantity.description: Copies to produce, at least 1, locked ones included.

Placement.description: A copy of a part, placed on a sheet or the strip.

oneOf.description:
Every copy of every part is placed. The expanded sheets are opened strictly in order, as a
prefix of the list, and the solver opens as few as possible. On the last opened sheet, the
parts are packed to the left and the sheet is cut vertically at
`LayoutStats::cut_x`, as far left as possible; the material right
of the cut is kept as a remnant. Every opened sheet but the last is used in full.

locked_parts.description: Placements that are given, which the solver completes.

sheets.description: The material, in the order it is used, nonempty.

oneOf.description:
One strip, from y = 0 to `height` and from x = 0 to the right without end. Every copy of every
part is placed, and the solver minimizes the length used,
`LayoutStats::cut_x`. The solution has one layout, whose
`sheet_id` is `"strip"`, or none when no part is placed. The boundary separation applies as for
a sheet, at the cut too.

locked_parts.description:
Placements that are given, which the solver completes, in strip coordinates; as for
`LockedLayout::placements`.

Project.description:
A client's project, stored with the account. Every response with a project carries its version
in an `ETag` header, which a save or deletion sends back in `If-Match`.

document.description: Opaque to the API: the client defines its format, and the API stores it as given.

ProjectSummary.description:
A project in a list, without its document; lists are ordered by `updated_at`, most recent
first.

ProjectSummaryList.description: One page of a list, ordered by the listed timestamp, ties broken by ID.

next_cursor.description: The cursor for the next page; `None` on the last page.

Reflection.description: A mirror of a geometry before it is rotated.

oneOf.description: Keeps the geometry as it is.
Mirrors the geometry across its own x-axis: (x, y) ↦ (x, −y).

Replay.description: What the search did, so that the same input, settings, threads, and build repeat it exactly.

oneOf.description:
A nonempty list of at most 65,536 angles; equivalent angles are merged, and 0° is not
implicit.

Run.description: How the job runs, known from its start.

Search.description:
The data of a `search` event, sent only with `EventsQuery::search`: the layout the search is
working on, which may be infeasible, at most 20 times a second. Best-effort: a job may send
none.

Segment.description: A piece of a `Contour::Path`, running from the previous segment's end to its own.

oneOf.description:
A circular arc. `bulge` is tan(θ/4) for the swept angle θ, positive counterclockwise, as
in DXF; `0` is a straight line. Its ends must differ: a full circle is a
`Contour::Circle` or two arcs.

Settings.description: How the solver ran on the input, including the values the service chose.

auto_termination.description: Whether the search ended early once it stopped improving.

time_limit_seconds.description: The maximum solver time, in whole seconds.

Shape.description:
One outer contour and any number of holes, which are regions without material.

In a part's geometry, each hole lies inside the outer contour; holes may touch it and each
other, but not overlap, and the material stays one connected piece. Otherwise the input is
invalid. In a sheet's geometry, holes are unusable regions without further rules: they may
reach outside the sheet, overlap, or split it into pieces.

SheetEntry.description:
Identical, anonymous sheets in a row. Sheets with different defects, or that must be told
apart, need separate entries.

defects.description:
Unusable regions in the sheet's coordinates, such as flaws or clamp areas. They may overlap
each other and reach outside the sheet.

quantity.description: How many sheets the entry expands to, at least 1.

Snapshot.description:
The data of a `snapshot` event on `GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}/events`: the best feasible solution
so far, at most 4 times a second and only when it improves. A `status` event carries the
`Job`.

sequence.description: Increases within the job; also the event's ID.

stats.description: The statistics the outcome would have if the job ended with this solution.

Solution.description: The placements per opened sheet; live snapshots carry solutions.

layouts.description: One layout per opened sheet, in the order the sheets are used.

solver_seconds.description: Solver time used, from the start of import, in whole seconds rounded up.

oneOf.description: Only a queued job is cancelled.

solver_seconds.description: Solver time used, as for a completed job; absent for a job that never started.

Stats.description: Statistics in total; `Stats::layouts` has them per layout.

Transformation.description:
Maps a part's original geometry onto its sheet:
p_sheet = R(`rotation`) · F(`reflection`) · p_geometry + `translation`,
about the geometry's own origin, which need not lie on or inside the shape. Every placement,
including a part inside another part's hole, is in sheet coordinates.

Unplaced.description: Copies of a part that were not placed.

bearer.description: An API key, a studio sign-in token, or an assistant's OAuth access token.

info.description: The job API of Sparrow Pro: submit nesting jobs, follow them live, and fetch their results; store projects for clients. Bodies are JSON, and requests may be gzip-compressed. Requests are read strictly: unknown fields and explicit nulls are refused, although these schemas do not say so. Responses are read tolerantly: clients ignore fields they do not know, and treat unknown values of open enumerations, such as error codes, diagnostic kinds, and termination reasons, as unknown. Every response carries an X-Request-Id header. See docs/job_api_contract.md and docs/io_format.md.
